NVIDIA.title: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance
NVIDIA.titleEn: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance
NVIDIA.summary:
In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation.
On the DeepSeek-V3 benchmark, Vera Rubin NVL72 scaled from 256 to 1,024 GPUs with about 97% efficiency: quadrupling the GPUs cut time to train from 16 minutes to about four.
NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power.

NVIDIA.title: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
NVIDIA.titleEn: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
NVIDIA.summary:
Cooler Optics, Replaceable Light Sources Increase Resiliency Lambda’s deployment uses NVIDIA Photonics switches, each with 144 ports running at 800Gb/s.
By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics.
The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.

Google DeepMind.titleEn: New AI training performance benchmarks for Google TPUs
Google DeepMind.summary:
Agentic RL on Ironwood: 640 Ironwood TPUs reached the target model’s coding benchmark target accuracy in 18.02 minutes (0.765 vs. the 0.69 goal), running code generation and learning simultaneously so training chips waited under 3% of the time.
Built on Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer architecture, these results reflect co-design across silicon, networking, and open software: Pre-training on Ironwood: 8,192 Ironwood TPUs reached the target model's benchmark target quality in 1.70 minutes, scaling up to 4,096 chips with 96% efficiency.

Ad Craig had a strategy to fix the phase by comparing progressively finer lattices, but couldn't prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover.
OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped produce a proof that could solve a 50-year-old problem in particle physics.

Writer.summary:
McKinsey reports that generative AI will propel $18-$30 billion in value annually through commercial life sciences (pharma) use cases like personalized content creation, medical and legal review assistance, customer enablement, strategic insights, and patient experience optimization.
With a generative AI platform, medical comms teams can reduce MLR review time from 30%-50%, increase first-pass MLR approvals by 20%-30%, and dramatically reduce the risk of fines and censure.
The same report predicts an additional $3 to $5 billion in annual value through efficiency gains in customer-insight generation, better-quality medical writing, and rapid summaries of scientific literature.

Writer.summary:
PubMed now indexes more than 1.56 million new citations a year , and scientific content is thought to be growing at roughly 5–6% annually .
While attitudes are beginning to shift toward human-in-the-loop approaches, relying on consumer-grade generative AI today can raise red flags during publication and peer review — exactly where credibility matters most.
But with more launches in narrower indications, tighter regulator and journal scrutiny, and stretched writing and review capacity, credibility can slip, not because the science is weak, but because the system can’t keep up.
